source.sampled_continuity: The 16-frame retained sheet is one continuous approach; the source title and later cut are outside the retained 3–9 s interval.

camera.method: Manually observed far-vessel screen drift, source-pose coordinates480×360. Does not disentangle moving distant ships from camera.

mask_fit.method: Filled native sail and hull compared against the nearest 12 fps SAM sample at 145 rendered frames; excludes drawn dinghy/reflection/background.
mask_fit.target_caveat: Main sail and hull broadly selected in sampled frames1,24,48; sample72 omits left hull. Model estimates are separate from measured filled-rig intersection-over-union.

assembly_summary: One real four-stroke sailboat approaches with its single sail left of an upright mast. The source has an additional right-hand jib that this doodle does not represent. A single distant-vessel plate follows measured screen drift; trailing dinghy is drawn by agent. No invented sail flutter.
review_note: Independent still review: original drawing identity passes; source framing/pose needs repair. Source pose: the prominent source sail spreads to both sides of the mast, whereas the rendered sail ends at the mast. In pairs 01 through 06 this omits a large right-hand part of the source silhouette and makes the boat read as a narrow single-sided sail rather than the source barge. The approach, hull placement, growth, and late frame exit otherwise track the source convincingly. The original QuickDraw identity remains legible in the triangular sail, doubled irregular mast, angular open-top hull, and unpolished thin contour. Normal-speed motion approval remains unrun. Three-round limit reached; remaining gap retained.
